entries.def: be effronted; to have a look of effrontery

1. to breathe again, take breath , (Iliad by Homer), etc.: to recover from a thing, with genitive, (Iliad by Homer), etc.; so, ἔκ τινος (Herdotus Historicus):—; absolute to revive , (Xenophon Historicus); and in this sense (Homer) uses ἄμπνυτο, ἀμπνύνθη. 
2. to draw breath, breathe , (Pindar) 
3. to breathe forth, send forth , καπνόν (Pindar) (ML)

1. recovery of breath, revival , (Pindar); μόχθων ἀμπνοά rest from toils, (Pindar) 
2. a drawing breath, respiration , (Aristophanes Comicus); ἀμπνοὰς ἔχειν = ἀναπνέειν, to breathe , (Sophocles Tragicus); τὴν ἀν. ἀπολαβεῖν τινος to strangle him. 
3. a breathing organ , of the mouth, (Lucian); an air-hole , (Plutarch) (ML)
to die in a place, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

1. properly of a bird, to raise its feathers : hence, ἀν. ἐθείρας (Euripides) 
2. metaphorically to set on the wing, excite vehemently , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; Pass. to be in a state of excitement , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. (ML)

1. to snatch up , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. to snatch away, carry off , (Homer), etc.; of slave-dealers, to kidnap , (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., (Sophocles Tragicus): in Prose also, to be dragged before a magistrate, carried off to prison , Lat. rapi in jus, (Demosthenes Orator) 
3. in good sense, to rescue , (Plutarch) 
4. to take by storm, plunder , (Euripides); of persons, ἀναρπασόμενος τοὺς Φωκέας to take them by…

1. to break up the ground, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. to break through a wall, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., ἡ ναῦς ἀναρρήγνυται τὴν παρεξειρεσίαν the ship has its bow broken through , (Thucydides) 
3. to tear open a carcase, of lions, (Iliad by Homer); of Ajax, δίχα ἀνερρήγνυ was cleaving them asunder, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. to make to break forth, utter , like Lat. rumpere voces, (Aristophanes Comicus); ἀν. πόλιν to make…
